issues.title: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
issues.reason: Root named: empty file makes json.load raise.

whys: load_notes does json.load with no guard.
frame.root: load_notes() in jot/cli.py raises on empty/bad file.
frame.best: Treat empty/invalid file as no notes (or clear error). One test.

repro.cmd: printf '' > factory/tmp/12.json; JOT_FILE=<repo>/factory/tmp/12.json python3 -m jot list
repro.out: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) (at jot/cli.py line 40 in load_notes, json.load(fh))

issues.details: Cause: load_notes() guards only a MISSING file (path.exists()); an existing-but-empty file falls through to json.load(fh), which raises JSONDecodeError on empty input instead of returning []. Any version, any OS. Fix: read text first, return [] when empty/whitespace.

rounds.fixer: load_notes reads text first; empty/whitespace/invalid -> [] instead of JSONDecodeError

issues.title: Notes file from Windows won't open on my Mac (UnicodeDecodeError 0xe9)
issues.reason: Root named: open() uses no explicit encoding.

frame.good: Yes. Cross-OS and emoji crashes share one cause.
whys: File read/written with the OS default codec.
Windows cp1252 can't do many chars.
frame.best: Open read+write with encoding='utf-8'. One test.

repro.cmd: write a latin-1 (0xe9) notes file; LC_ALL=C JOT_FILE=<repo>/factory/tmp/16.json python3 -m jot list
repro.out: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe9 in position 23: invalid continuation byte (at jot/cli.py line 40, json.load(fh))
repro.note: byte 0xe9 ('é') from a cp1252/latin-1 file fails UTF-8 decode

issues.details: Cause: load_notes() calls open(path) with no encoding= argument, so Python uses the platform/locale default. A notes file written by a Windows editor in cp1252/latin-1 (byte 0xe9) is not valid UTF-8 and the read raises UnicodeDecodeError. save_notes writes with no explicit encoding too. Fix: open read+write with encoding='utf-8'.

issues.title: IDs are reused after deleting a note

frame.good: Yes. The clearest statement of the id bug.

repro.cmd: jot add a; add b; add c; rm 2; add d; list (JOT_FILE=<repo>/factory/tmp/32.json)
repro.out:
added 1
added 2
added 3
rm 2
added 3
[ ] 1 a
[ ] 3 c
[ ] 3 d
repro.note: new note d reuses id 3 (still held by c)

issues.details: Cause: next_id() returns len(notes)+1. rm shrinks the list, so the count-based id collides with a still-present note's id. Any version, any OS. Fix: monotonic counter (max existing id + 1, or a persisted seq).

issues.title: JOT_FILE with ~ creates a folder literally named ~

repro.out:
added 1
./~  (a directory literally named ~ created in CWD; $HOME path not created)

issues.details: Cause: notes_path() does Path(env) on JOT_FILE with no expanduser(). A caller (or shell) that does not expand the ~ passes it literally, so jot makes a directory literally named '~' in the CWD instead of writing under $HOME. Any version; POSIX + Windows. Fix: Path(os.path.expanduser(env)).

issues.title: Tags typed with # show as ##work and can't be filtered
issues.reason: Root: '#work' stored verbatim, shown as ##work.

whys: jot stores it and prepends # on show.

repro.cmd: jot add 'fix the parser' --tag '#work'; jot list; jot list --tag work; jot list --tag '#work' (JOT_FILE=<repo>/factory/tmp/67.json)
repro.out:
[ ] 1 ... fix the parser  ##work
(--tag work -> no output)
(--tag '#work' -> matches ##work)
repro.note: leading # doubled on display; plain 'work' filter misses it

issues.details: Cause: add_note() stores tag strings verbatim (sorted(set(tags))), so '#work' keeps its leading '#'; format_note() prepends another '#' giving '##work', and filter_notes() does an exact-string match so filtering by the name 'work' returns nothing. Fix: strip a leading # on add (normalise tags).

issues.title: BrokenPipeError when I pipe jot list into head
issues.reason: Piping to head raises BrokenPipeError.

frame.best: Catch BrokenPipe and exit quietly. One test.

repro.cmd: seed 5000 notes; JOT_FILE=<repo>/factory/tmp/73.json python3 -m jot list 2>73.err | head -n 1
repro.out:
[ ] 1 ... note number 1
...
BrokenPipeError: [Errno 32] Broken pipe (at jot/cli.py line 135 in main, print(format_note(note))); list exit 1
repro.note: head closes the pipe, traceback + exit 1

issues.details: Cause: main()'s 'list' branch prints each note in a loop with no BrokenPipeError guard; when a downstream reader (head) closes the pipe before all notes are written, print() raises BrokenPipeError, which escapes main() as a traceback and exit 1 instead of a clean exit. Fix: catch BrokenPipe and exit quietly.

issues.title: `jot list --tag work` misses notes tagged Work
issues.reason: Root named: --tag match is case-sensitive.

frame.good: Yes. Work vs work splits a user's notes.
whys: Case differs between entry and query.
frame.best: Fold case when matching tags. One test.

repro.cmd: jot add 'ship it' --tag Work; jot add 'review PR' --tag work; jot list --tag work (JOT_FILE=<repo>/factory/tmp/76.json)
repro.out:
added 1
added 2
[ ] 2 ... review PR  #work   (the 'Work' note is missed)
repro.note: --tag work returns only the lowercase-tagged note

issues.details: Cause: filter_notes() tests `tag not in note['tags']`, an exact case-sensitive string match; a note tagged 'Work' is skipped when filtering '--tag work'. add_note stores tags verbatim with no case normalisation. Fix: fold case when matching tags.

issues.title: jot search doesn't find notes by their tag
issues.reason: Works as designed: search is text-only by its docstring. Reframe as a feature: extend search to tags.

frame.good: Yes. Users expect search to see tags.
whys: search_notes reads only text ('Plain substring match').
Tags are a separate field, ignored by design.
frame.root: search ignores the tags field -- documented behaviour, not a defect.
frame.best: Search text and tags. One flag-free change, one test.

repro.cmd: jot add 'buy milk' --tag errands; jot search errands (JOT_FILE=<repo>/factory/tmp/95.json)
